---
title: Write safely
description: Change an item without overwriting someone else's change, settle a conflict when one happens, create an item only once, and retry a write without making it twice.
---

Another app, agent or device may change an item between your read and your write. **Every update names the version it read,** so Marfa can tell, and it never lets a stale write overwrite a newer change unseen. [Versions](/build/versions) explains what a version counts.

In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. An app on the Swift SDK writes through a working copy, which sends each write and settles its conflicts for you ([Devices](/build/devices)).

## Send the version you read

Read the item, change what you need, and send the `version` you read with **only the properties you changed**. They're laid over the item's own:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 1 --prop body="Take the train from Porto, then the tram."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1, "properties": { "body": "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  body: { version: 1, properties: { body: "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } },
});
```

An update without a version is refused `400 missing_required_field`, since Marfa couldn't tell whether it was stale. [Update an item](/api-reference/items/updateItem) lists the other fields an update takes.

Marfa answers in one of four ways:

| Answer | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` at the next version | Nobody changed the item since you read it. | Keep the item in the answer. |
| `200` further along | Someone changed other fields since. Marfa laid your change over theirs. | Replace your copy with the item in the answer: it holds both. |
| `200` with `acknowledged: true` | The write would leave the item as it is. | Nothing. Marfa stores no version and sends no event. |
| `409 version_conflict` | Someone changed a field you changed. | Settle it, as the next two sections show. |

A write refused for any other reason, such as properties that don't fit the type, is in [Fix a refused write](/build/fix-a-refused-write).

## Settle a conflict yourself

Here another app changed the body after you read version 1. The refusal carries **`current`**, the item now, **`ancestor`**, the item at the version you read, and **`conflicting_fields`**, the fields both writes changed:

```json title="Response" status="409"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "version_conflict",
    "message": "Version 1 is stale; current version is 2. Conflicting fields: body."
  },
  "current": {
    "id": "01a1f122-fe33-7556-98c7-99bc8e30b659",
    "version": 2,
    "properties": { "title": "Lisbon trip", "body": "Take the morning train from Porto." }
  },
  "ancestor": {
    "id": "01a1f122-fe33-7556-98c7-99bc8e30b659",
    "version": 1,
    "properties": { "title": "Lisbon trip", "body": "Take the train from Porto." }
  },
  "conflicting_fields": ["body"],
  "merge_policy": { "fields": { "body": "keep_both_copies", "notes": "keep_both_copies" }, "default": "last_writer_wins" }
}
```

The response above is shortened. The CLI prints the message and exits `1`, and the TypeScript SDK hands back the body as `error`.

For each conflicting field, compare your value with `ancestor` and `current`, and choose: keep one, combine them, or show both to the person. A conflict can name `tier`, `occurred_at`, `source_id` or `type` as well as properties. Then **send your choice at the version in `current`**:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 2 --prop body="Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 2, "properties": { "body": "Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  body: { version: 2, properties: { body: "Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram." } },
});
```

If someone writes again first, the same refusal comes back. After a few tries, show the person the conflict.

## Let Marfa settle it

Add `conflict=auto`, and Marfa **settles each colliding field by the type's merge policy** instead of refusing. `auto` is the only value `conflict` takes:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 1 --conflict auto --prop body="Take the train from Porto, then the tram."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>?conflict=auto
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 1, "properties": { "body": "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id }, query: { conflict: "auto" } },
  body: { version: 1, properties: { body: "Take the train from Porto, then the tram." } },
});
```

A [merge policy](/catalog/type-rules#merge-policy) gives each field one of two strategies:

- **`last_writer_wins`** takes your value.
- **`keep_both_copies`** keeps the value the item holds and writes yours to a **conflicted copy**: a new item of the same type, tagged `conflicted-copy`, with a `derived-from` edge to the original. `core.note` keeps both copies of its `body` and `notes`.

The answer is `200` with the item, and `conflict_resolution` beside it says what Marfa did:

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "conflict_resolution": {
    "fields": ["body"],
    "strategy": { "body": "keep_both_copies" },
    "conflicted_copy_id": "01a1f122-dfe4-74e8-9396-986ca176a78a"
  }
}
```

The response above is shortened. **`conflicted_copy_id` is the only place the copy's ID appears**, so keep it or show the person the copy. Marfa doesn't settle a write that collides and also moves the item to another type: that one is refused `409 version_conflict` for you to settle.

## When Marfa no longer holds your version

Marfa compares a stale write against its snapshot of the version you read, and it thins old snapshots. A long-held edit can name a version it no longer has, and is then refused `409 ancestor_unavailable`, whatever `conflict` says. The refusal carries `current` and the `requested_version` you sent.

**Make your change again on top of `current`,** and send it at the version `current` holds. Sending your old values at the new version would undo whatever arrived since.

## Create an item only once

A create that names a `source_id` its source already holds **updates that item** instead of adding one. To create the item or change nothing, as an agent that may repeat itself should, add `mode: "create_only"`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items create --type core.bookmark --source-id lisbon-guide --create-only \
  --prop title="Lisbon guide" --prop url=https://example.com/lisbon
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.bookmark",
  "source_id": "lisbon-guide",
  "mode": "create_only",
  "properties": { "title": "Lisbon guide", "url": "https://example.com/lisbon" }
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
  body: {
    type: "core.bookmark",
    source_id: "lisbon-guide",
    mode: "create_only",
    properties: { title: "Lisbon guide", url: "https://example.com/lisbon" },
  },
});
```

If an item holds that `source_id` or the `id` you sent, live or in the bin, Marfa **writes nothing** and answers `409 item_exists`, with the item in `details.existing_id` and `source_id` or `id` in `details.matched_by`. To change that item, read it and [send the version you read](#send-the-version-you-read). [Upsert items in bulk](/api-reference/items/bulkUpsertItems) takes the same `mode` and reports such an entry `skipped`.

## Retry with an Idempotency-Key

When you can't tell whether a write landed, because the connection dropped or Marfa answered `429 rate_limited` or a `5xx`, send it again. Give each write an `Idempotency-Key` header with a fresh unique value, such as a UUID, and **send the same key with the retry**:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items update <id> --version 2 --idempotency-key 0199a9d1-4e5f-7a6b-9c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d \
  --prop body="Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram."
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Idempotency-Key: 0199a9d1-4e5f-7a6b-9c7d-8e9f0a1b2c3d
Content-Type: application/json

{ "version": 2, "properties": { "body": "Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram." } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

const key = randomUUID();
const send = () =>
  marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
    params: { path: { id }, header: { "Idempotency-Key": key } },
    body: { version: 2, properties: { body: "Take the morning train from Porto, then the tram." } },
  });
```

If Marfa already answered that request, it **returns the first answer again** with the header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and writes nothing. It keeps the answer as long as it keeps the event log, 30 days by default. It keeps no answer of `401`, `403` or a `5xx`, so a repeat of one of those runs again.

**A key names one request.** The same key on another request, such as your settled write after a conflict, is refused `422 idempotency_key_reused`. A repeat that arrives while the first is still running is refused `409 idempotency_key_in_flight`: wait, then send it again. [Errors](/api-reference/errors#retrying) says which refusals to retry.

A write to one item, its tags or its extensions takes a key, and so do edge, folder and view writes, [Apply a bulk action](/api-reference/bulk-actions/applyBulkAction) and a row batch and its undo ([Tables](/build/tables)). [Upsert items in bulk](/api-reference/items/bulkUpsertItems) takes none: give each entry a `source_id`, and a repeat updates the same items, or reports an entry `skipped` as `unchanged`.

The rules are in the contract's [versions](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/versions.md) chapter and its [idempotency keys](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md#idempotency-keys).
